Dear Sir or Madam,

Thank you for your enquiry. Please find our Angebot below.

We offer a price of €438.21 per unit, a volume of 4580 pcs per year, a contract term of 12 months, and a Zahlungsziel 30 days net. This offer remains valid for 30 days.

Regarding our cost structure, CU-NOTATION rose 47.7 % in twelve months and is 5 % of our cost. LCI-C rose 2.7 % in twelve months and is 16 % of our cost. Furthermore, PPI-C2611 rose 13.5 % in twelve months and is 42 % of our cost.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Birgit Mayrhofer
Key Account Manager, Selvbrunn Drive Systems GmbH

move.subject: Re: Quote from Selvbrunn Drive Systems GmbH: Frame agreement renewal for the 7.5 kW frequency converter
move.body:
Dear Sir or Madam,

Thank you for your offer and for explaining your position.
Thank you for your note on renewing our framework agreement for the frequency converter; we value our long and reliable partnership. We understand the pressure on electronic components and copper, and we respect your head office's pricing framework. As you asked, we are sharing our expected volumes, which are growing, and we propose a binding volume over a two-year term together with early call-offs around your shutdown. In return we would like to keep the price stable.

Our data shows a different picture on some points:
Our demand forecast for this part has risen 10.3% (fc:350020@2026-09).
Our latest orders for this part were all at EUR 412.74 per unit (po:4500014465-10, po:4500014417-10, po:4500014351-10).
Your rolling scorecard shows on-time delivery of 84.6% (sc:70530@2026Q3).

Please find our proposal below.

We look forward to your reply.

Kind regards
Purchasing
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH

move.text:
Dear Sir or Madam,
Thank you for your e-mail, which we have reviewed internally.
We can accept your terms and await your order.
Our terms: a price of €433.05 per unit, Zahlungsziel 90 days net, a volume of 4580 pcs per year, a contract term of 24 months.
Please note:
We checked the price history data you cited; it holds, but it does not change our calculation.
We checked the volume change data you cited; it holds and we took it into account.
As to the delivery record and price history and volume change data you cited, our management has frozen all price reductions until December 2027. We can talk about the terms instead - payment, volume or contract length.
We welcome your proposal for a 24-month contract, which enables us to offer a more favorable unit price.
While we note your historical purchase price and delivery records, our current pricing strictly reflects the updated material costs we have absorbed.
Our price follows our main cost drivers: PPI-C2611, LCI-C, CU-NOTATION.
This offer is subject to our general terms of sale.
Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Birgit Mayrhofer
Key Account Manager, Selvbrunn Drive Systems GmbH

key_points: Selvbrunn is our sole active source for a strategic A-part. It is sound, and we are a small customer to it, so posturing or switch threats would backfire.
Head office has frozen price reductions, and any change above two percent goes to the pricing committee. Aim for a flat price, or an increase small enough to stay inside the front line's authority.
They asked for volumes: answer with our rising forecast and a binding volume equal to our real need, plus a twenty-four-month term covering the freeze period.
The current price sits near our no-margin should-cost, and the margin charge applies on this stabilise part. Do not squeeze it hard; land near flat.
Payment days are our closing concession. They value short payment, so keep thirty days or offer fourteen as the last step, and never ask for longer terms.
Hold the delivery shortfall back as a fresh argument for a later round, framed as a joint improvement topic.
Never cite index rises, the Konvertek quote or Selvbrunn's quality record.
Evidence on Selvbrunn's actual cost is thin.
plan.stance_why: This is a strategic sole source under a reduction freeze, with the price close to our no-margin should-cost and a margin charge on stabilise parts. Our fallback is far dearer and slower. Opening near their price keeps them inside front-line authority, so they can close without a committee cycle.

levers.why: Answers their volume request with checkable growth and supports a binding volume.

argument.sentence: Our demand forecast for this part has risen 10.3% (fc:350020@2026-09).
argument.note: Snapshot 2026-09: 4580 for the next 12 months against 4154 ordered in the last 12 months (requested dates); shared with suppliers: True. More volume is worth more to it.

levers.why: Anchors continuity at the current price, which is checkable.

argument.sentence: Our latest orders for this part were all at EUR 412.74 per unit (po:4500014465-10, po:4500014417-10, po:4500014351-10).
argument.note: What we pay now: [412.74, 412.74, 412.74] per unit (2026-08-31 to 2026-09-28); anchors any increase.

levers.why: Shows we respect their shutdown planning and will place early January call-offs.

argument.sentence: We refer to your e-mail "Holiday shutdown" (doc:20251201-70530-N).
argument.note: email 2025-12-01 by Selvbrunn Drive Systems GmbH: Our plant is closed from 23 December to 6 January. Please place call-offs for January by 10 December.

levers.why: A fresh, true fact for a later round, framed as joint improvement against the delivery target.

argument.sentence: Your rolling scorecard shows on-time delivery of 84.6% (sc:70530@2026Q3).
argument.note: Rolling 12 months to 2026-09-30: 84.6% on time against the requested date (84.6% against its own confirmed date); target 95%; peers' median 84.6%; class A green. A year earlier 88.0%.

levers.why: Links the delivery shortfall to the agreed target in the quality agreement.

argument.sentence: Our framework agreement includes the quality agreement with its delivery target.
argument.note: ctr:4600070530#6.1 (quality): The quality agreement applies: on-time delivery target 95 %, flat fee of EUR 150 per supplier-caused complaint.

levers.why: Shows their renewals usually settle well below the ask.

argument.note: 3 renewals: asked +2.1% on average, settled -0.1% (gap 2.2 pp); last 2025-11-21: asked +5.5%, settled +3.1%. It usually settles well below its ask.

levers.why: Shows we are a reliable payer, which supports the payment trade.

argument.note: 72 invoices; we pay 2.0 days after due on average (last 12 months), 74.3% late, 0.0% over 10 days late, max 7; discounts taken 0 (0 after the period); short-paid 0. We pay reliably: a fair customer.

levers.why: Use only to show the current price already covers cost, never as a lever for a cut.

argument.sentence: Our bottom-up cost model puts the full cost of this part at EUR 403.21 per unit (cost:350020).
argument.note: Should-cost EUR 403.21 per unit (its own plant, error about 5%); its price EUR 412.74 per unit (price from 2026-01-01) is +2.4% against it.

trades.why: A binding volume equal to our real need gives them the planning security they asked for.
Twenty-four months captures the value of length and covers their freeze period.
Keeps the current thirty days, which they value, and costs us nothing new.
Faster payment as the final step instead of a price increase.

sup:70530.opening_paragraph: Thank you for your note on renewing our framework agreement for the frequency converter; we value our long and reliable partnership. We understand the pressure on electronic components and copper, and we respect your head office's pricing framework. As you asked, we are sharing our expected volumes, which are growing, and we propose a binding volume over a two-year term together with early call-offs around your shutdown. In return we would like to keep the price stable.
watch_for: A demand for an index clause set at the current peaks: decline it, or accept only at a base well below the fixed price.
Any increase above the committee threshold, which delays each round by about two weeks.
A hold or final offer: under the freeze they move once, so close quickly or switch to the faster-payment trade.
Use of our should-cost figure to claim they sell at cost.
A request for faster payment: keep fourteen days for the closing step.
An auto-renewal reference: we must decide internally before the termination deadline.

risks: Squeezing the price risks the margin charge and harms a sole-source relationship.
Their increase claim may exceed the committee threshold and drag out the timeline.
Auto-renewal at the old terms if the notice deadline passes; this may even be acceptable.
Little hard evidence of Selvbrunn's actual cost, so our arguments rest mainly on volume and terms.
Their delivery shortfall could threaten our lead-time need regardless of price.
